title: Power Display: Setting contrast to 0 causes black screen
summary: Setting contrast to zero turns one reported Power Display monitor black.

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied the precise value and monitor model, permitting a controlled maintainer comparison; device behavior and an appropriate guard remain uncertain.
evidence: On 0.99.1 the reporter says setting contrast to zero blacks the screen while the application continues; moving the slider restores it.
The reporter identified the affected monitor as a SANC G52 Plus IPS.
MonitorViewModel.SetContrastAsync clamps to 0–100 and passes the chosen value to the hardware manager; that does not prove how every display renders zero.
judgment.recommended_action: Safely compare the monitor’s native behavior and Power Display behavior before considering a warning or recovery affordance.

fix_assessment.rationale: A device-safe warning or reversible change may be warranted after behavior and recovery are characterized; arbitrary universal clamping is not justified.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate safe contrast adjustment and recovery
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The device may legitimately produce an all-black image at its minimum contrast; whether Power Display creates additional unrecoverable risk is unknown.
plan: Safely reproduce on the reported or comparable display and compare the monitor’s own minimum setting.
Determine whether an accessible recovery path or confirmation is needed for potentially unreadable values.
Design any warning or timed revert without imposing an unverified universal minimum, and consider saved settings and CLI paths.
Test restoration, cancellation, multi-monitor behavior and monitors whose minimum is safe.
verification: A user can recover from a display becoming unreadable without relying on the affected display.
Supported monitor contrast ranges and intentional low values remain available according to the agreed design.

confidence.rationale: The observed value and hardware are known, but current behavior and whether a cross-device warning or recovery design is justified are unverified.

issue_context.summary: Setting contrast to zero turns one reported Power Display monitor black.
known_information: On 0.99.1 the reporter says setting contrast to zero blacks the screen while the application continues; moving the slider restores it.
The reporter identified the affected monitor as a SANC G52 Plus IPS.
inferences: A device may legitimately interpret minimum contrast as black; the appropriate protection and affected monitor range are not established.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/PowerDisplay/PowerDisplay/ViewModels/MonitorViewModel.cs: SetContrastAsync permits 0 and delegates the hardware write.
Reviewed complete issue discussion including the answered monitor-model question, no assignee and no timeline fix.
Searched open upstream PR titles for contrast work; no covering Power Display fix was established.
issue_context.analysis: The report gives an actionable hardware-specific scenario. Reproduction must have an independently operable recovery path and should not assume a universal safe minimum.

information_gaps.information: Whether the affected device’s own controls also render zero black and what recovery options exist on current Power Display.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes hardware semantics from a Power Display-specific defect and informs a safe warning or recovery design.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer uses a recoverable monitor test setup and compares the device’s native control with Power Display.

reproduce.title: Compare monitor and Power Display contrast
reproduce.version_requirement: Use the current PowerToys release; report was on 0.99.1.
prerequisites: Use a test monitor with known physical on-screen controls or a separately visible display and verified recovery method; do not perform this on an only display without recovery.
setup: Record the original contrast value and verify that the monitor hardware controls or separate display can restore it.
steps: 1. On the test monitor, compare the native on-screen contrast control at a low setting and restore the original value.
2. With the verified independent recovery available, set contrast to zero through Power Display and observe the image.
3. Restore the original value immediately using the independent control and verify display usability.
4. Repeat with another compatible monitor only if it can be recovered independently.
reproduce.expected_result: The monitor remains recoverable and the behavior at minimum is understood without assuming all devices share one safe value.
